title: Compressed-weight variant intake and accuracy watchdog for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Create an intake + validation pipeline and a production 'accuracy watchdog' that accepts compressed-weight model variants (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ), verifies calibration and functional parity against pinned reference versions, and publishes a joined artifact that the serving runtime and console can consume. This ticket covers: (1) a manifest/variant-index schema for compressed weights and associated metadata, (2) an automated offline validation harness that runs accuracy and latency checks, (3) CI gating that rejects variants with regressions beyond thresholds, (4) runtime hooks for drift detection and automatic fallback to a pinned compatible variant, and (5) UI surface in Console for published variant status and recent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Variant manifest schema v1 published and documented in Confluence (fields: base_model_hash, quant_type, quant_params, calibration_seed, sample_prompts_hash, build_artifact_url, checksum, estimated_tokens_per_second)
Offline validation harness executes for new artifact uploads and completes within 45 minutes for a standard 7B model on our CI workers
Regression detection rules: <= 2% absolute drop on normalized generation-quality score OR <= 5% drop on embedding-cosine against baseline will mark as 'rejected'
Latency / p95 token time vs baseline documented; any >30% increase triggers caution flag but not automatic reject
CI gate in model-publish pipeline (GitHub PR) that fails on rejected artifacts and annotates PR with dashboard links
Canary rollout policy implemented: shadow traffic for 5k inferences, then progressive ramp at 10%, 30%, 60% with rollback condition if watchdog fires
Console shows variant status (GREEN/YELLOW/RED), last-run summary, and links to diffed example outputs and ROC/metric timelines
Alerting: PagerDuty on high-severity perf regressions; low-severity alerts to #runtime-ops Slack channel
updates: 2026-02-18 - Ticket created by Aisha Khan: initial scope drafted after model-onboarding sync. Noted need to avoid duplicate artifacts and to unify manifest fields across quant engines.
2026-02-22 - Architecture sync: decided manifest is canonical single source; storage in S3 under /variants/<model>/<version>/manifest.json. Marco volunteered to prototype schema and validation tool.

2026-02-27 - Trade-off discussion: AWQ shows non-deterministic token-level variability in some runs. Decided to add worked examples and expanded promptset that emphasizes long-context behavior for AWQ variants.

2026-03-03 - Engineering update (Marco): initial harness implemented (github.com/redwood-inference/variant-validator PR #612). Harness runs accuracy/embedding/latency checks and emits a JSON report. Still missing CI integration.
2026-03-06 - PM feedback (Priya Patel): request to include customer-facing summary strings and an opt-out toggle for enterprise customers during private deployments.
2026-03-09 - Observability (Ethan Brooks): dashboard prototype created (internal link) showing rolling 24h generation-quality, embedding drift, and token-latency. Added sample alert thresholds.

2026-03-12 - Decision: gating thresholds tightened after small internal canary revealed a 3.8% embedding drop for GPTQ baseline case. Adjusted rule to normalized generation-quality <=2% OR embedding-cosine <=4.5% as rejection criteria. Updated CI gate PR #634 linked.
2026-03-12 - Next: integrate runtime fallback hook (engine side) and add a small audit trail in Console for who approved variant publication. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2026-03-22.
notes: Implementation notes: keep manifest intentionally minimal to enable future extension (use short kebab-case keys). Use content-addressed base_model_hash to detect identical upstream FP16/FP32 bases.
Calibration matrix: for INT8/FP8 include per-layer calibration_stats and a condensed summary to keep artifact size < 50MB for the UI; full stats stored in S3 with signed URL.
Performance considerations: offline re-calibration runs can be CPU-heavy; schedule heavy jobs on dedicated calibration workers to avoid noisy neighbor effects on CI.
Rollback strategy: immediate runtime fallback to last-green variant; generate postmortem and disable auto-publish for that model family until root cause analysis.
Open question: whether to include model-specific tokenizer-normalization diffs in the validation report; opted to capture tokenization checksum for now.
Cross-team ask: security should validate the artifact ingestion S3 path and ensure KMS policies for private deployments. Invite Sandra Kim from Security for final review before GA.
